text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- In a historic celebration in the south of the Nile valley, President Hosni Mubarak saw the first drop of water flow from Lake Nasser into the Toshka canal in preparation for progress towards the "dream" national project to build a second valley parallel to the Nile valley. Mubarak said there was no time to waste for the 21st century is approaching and Egypt must be ready to absorb new Egyptians, give them a livelihood and make the transformation from living on four percent of the land area to living on 25 percent.
- Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will have talks in Cairo today on the Middle East peace process.
Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti is also coming, with a message from King Hussein.

- Health Minister Ismail Sallam said there were no cases of meningitis among schoolchildren and there was no justification for the rush to get hold of meningitis vaccine. But a ministry official said the ministry was taking all the usual precautions and was vaccinating children against meningitis.

- Culture Minister Farouk Hosni has sent a team to London to follow the court case over the return of 74 Egyptian antiquities seized by British police in 1993. Egypt says they were taken out of Egypt illegally.

- Tourism Minister Mamdouh el-Beltagi, in interview with al-Ahram Hebdo, says tourism cooperation with Israel will remain suspended until stability returns to the region. He said the recent tension will affect the number of tourists.
AL-AKHBAR
- Mubarak speaks at Toshka ceremony.
- A senior Jordanian official said there would be a four-way meeting between Mubarak, Arafat, Netanyahu and King Hussein.
- Egypt has signed the nuclear test ban treaty.
- The Council of State has approved the Interior Minister's decision to give foreigners residence for longer periods.

- The general assembly of the Holding Company for Housing, Cinema and Tourism has agreed to sell 75 percent of al-Ahram Beverages to a group of Egyptian and U.S. investors at 74 pounds a share, making a total of 285 million pounds ($84 million), without the land and buildings, which they could use only for the first five years. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said the central audit office had assessed the company at 253 million pounds with land and buildings. The investors are committed to keep on the workforce and will invest 150 million to modernise the company.
- Two young girls die in Qena after circumcision operation and are buried without a permit.
- A madman caused a stir at the U.S. embassy when he turned up and demanded to meet Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Mubarak says: "This is where the new valley begins."
- Contracts will be signed with applicants for mobile phones from October 25 onwards and the service will begin on November 1. Trials have gone well and the system in Cairo can handle 70,000 lines.
$1 = 3.4 Egyptian pounds
